question: Should this draft be accepted as the retrospective design record for the shipped `openclaw backup sqlite` capability, or should the repository avoid adding an RFC after implementation has already landed?
rationale: The code/docs demonstrate that the central Phase 1 capability exists, but only maintainers can decide whether an accepted RFC adds durable architectural value now and what implementation issue or discussion should be its provenance.

options.title: Sponsor a retrospective RFC
options.body: Create or link the maintainer discussion and implementation issue, update the RFC to the current `openclaw backup sqlite` contract, then accept it before merge.

options.title: Keep it as a draft
options.body: Leave the proposal open until a maintainer wants the RFC record and can supply the required acceptance context.

options.title: Close the draft
options.body: Close it if the shipped backup documentation and implementation history are the preferred record of this already-landed design.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a retrospective RFC
recommendation.body: Create or link the maintainer discussion and implementation issue, update the RFC to the current `openclaw backup sqlite` contract, then accept it before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence owner fallback for deciding whether a retrospective RFC is warranted.
